Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 14175 of 2025
Applicant :- Chhotu

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Durgesh Chandra Tiwari,Krishna Murari Tripathi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1. Heard Sri Krishna Murari Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri S.P. learned State Law Officer for the State.
2. This Court on 25.04.2025 issued notices to respondent nos.2 to 3 and there is an office report dated 22.05.2025 that the notices has been served upon the opposite party no.2 & 3.

Till the dictation of the order, nobody has put in appearance on behalf of opposite party no.2.
3.

The case of the applicant is that proceedings U/s 156 (3) Cr.P.C. was lodged by the opposite party no.2 on 19.01.2022 against the applicant with an allegation that the opposite party no.2/
complainant is a labour of a down trodden community.

The allegations is that the opposite party no.2- husband is out of station in connection with his work and so far as the applicant is concerned,
he happens to be not of a good conduct.

Further allegations is that on 16.12.2021 at 6:00 in the evening when the daughter of the opposite party no.2, victim aged about 16 year had gone out of the house to answer the natures call but she did not return and on 27.12.2021 at 4:00 in the evening the applicant left victim outside the house of the opposite party no.2 and ran away.

When the enquiry was made, regarding the absence of the victim then she stated that on 16.12.2021 when the victim had gone to answer the natures call then the applicant herein caught hold of her and committed bad act while threatening that the opposite party n.2 would be done to death if she disclosed the said act and he would continue to commit the bad act in future also.
As per the complaint, the matter was reported to the police station, however, the police did not register the FIR.

The constant efforts were Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135374037/
1 made for getting the FIR lodged and on 03.01.2022 the police showed its reluctance to lodge the FIR pursuant whereto on 05.01.2022 a register complaint was sent to the SSP.

sentences.text: However, nothing was done so on 19.01.2022 the complaint was lodged.

Thereafter on 07.02.2022 the court of Additional Sessions Judge, Special Judge (POCSO court) Sonbhadra proceeded to pass an order treating the case to be a complaint case and the statement of the opposite party no.2 was recorded U/s 200 Cr.P.C. followed by the statement of witnesses namely Kamal Khan, Geeta Devi U/s 202 Cr.P.C. and of the victim also under Section 202 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Special Judge (POCSO court) Sonbhadra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Post recording of the statement on 11.08.2022 the applicant has been summoned U/s 376 (2)(N), 344, 506 IPC read with Section 5 (L) (N) of the POCSO Act.
4. Questioning the summoning order, the applicant has filed the present application.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the summoning order cannot be sustained for a single moment for more than one reason.

Firstly, there has been a delay in lodging of the proceedings particularly when the incident is to be dated 16.12.2021 but the proceedings U/s 156 (3)
Cr.P.C was drawn on 19.01.2022.

Secondly, there happens to be a police report wherein it was found that the applicant is nephew of the complainant and pressure was being mounted by the opposite party no.2 to the complainant for getting the marriage of the victim solemnized with the applicant and when the applicant showed its reluctance then a false story is being sought to be implanted which transformed into the summoning order.
Thirdly, the victim was not been subjected to any medical examination and had it been the case, the entire facts would have surfaced showing the falsity in the allegations so made against him.

Fourthly, the victim itself is a major girl, however on the basis of the mark sheet of class-VIII the age has been determined which was made the basis of holding the applicant to be victim which is not as per section 94 of Juvinile Justice Care and Protection of Child Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvinile Justice Care and Protection of Child Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He submits that what would be relevant would be ossification test or if the victim is a student of class X high school certificate.
He thus submits that the summoning order cannot be sustained and it is liable to be sustained.

6. Learned State Law Officer on the other hand submits that whatever might be presumption U/s 29 of the POCSO Act would be there and further there are no major or material contradiction in the statement U/s 200 & 202 Cr.P.C. vis-a-vis, the complaint and thus it may not be appropriate to throttle the investigation at this stage.
7.
I have heard the submissions so made across the bar and perused the record carefully.

8. Apparently in the present case at hand at the instance of the applicant, challenge has been raised to an order of summoning the applicant under section 376 (2)(N), 344, 506 IPC read with Section 5(L)/ 6 of the POCSO Act.
There are certain parameters which would be material in order to determine as to whether the summoning order suffers from illegality or not.

Amongst others one of the criteria inevitably would be allegations in the complaint vis-a-vis the statement of the witnesses U/s 200 & 202 of the Cr.P.C. Applying the said principles in the facts and the circumstances of the case, the Court finds that there happens to be a complaint dated 19.01.2022 lodged by the mother of the victim/ complainant against the applicant with relation to outraging the modesty and committing bad act on 16.12.2021.

In her statement U/s 200 Cr.P.C. has supported the prosecution Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135374037/
2 theory so much so, the witnesses U/s 202 Cr.P.C. being Kamal Khan and Geeta Devi have also supported the prosecution theory.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A conjoint reading of the statement of U/s 200 of the complainant and of the statement of witnesses U/s 202 Cr.P.C. has referred to above would reveal that they stick to the allegation dated 16.12.2021, the victim's modesty were outraged and she was subjected to bad act.
On top of it, the statement U/s 202 Cr.P.C. of the victim is also crucial wherein she has deposed that bad act has been committed by the applicant on 16.12.2021.

So far as the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that there happens to be the delay in lodging of the complaint particularly when the complaint stood lodged on 19.1.2022 and the incident is dated 16.12.2021 is concerned, the same may be a factor to be considered at the stage when a decision is to be taken whether the accused is to be convicted or acquitted but the same cannot be sole ground to throttle the investigation as its strength is to be evaluated when the trial commences.

With respect to the contention raised by the counsel for the applicant that there happens to be a police report mentioning therein that the applicant happens to be the nephew of the complainant and the basic factor which motivated the lodging of the criminal proceedings is the refusal of the applicant not to get marriage solemnized with the victim is concerned
, the same may be at best at defence, stage of consideration whereof would only arise when the trial commences.
The import and the impact and the effect of the police report is not to be adjudged or adjudicated at the stage of summoning.

Moreover, so far as the objection raised by the counsel for the applicant that the victim was not subjected to medical examination is concerned and had the victim being subjected to medical examination the truth would have surfaced is concerned, this court at the stage of challenge being raised to the summoning is not required to delve into the said factual aspect as the same may be a ground which might have its own strength and effect when the trial commences when a decision is to be taken either for conviction or acquittal.

In so far as the argument raised by the counsel for the applicant that on the basis of the marksheet of class VIII the age of the victim has been determined to be 16 years being minor and in absence of any ossification or any other method, the penal provision under POCSO Act could not have been invoked is concerned, this Court is not required to go into the said aspect of the matter as the same would occasion leading of evidences stage whereof has not arisen till date.
Moreover, what is more relevant is the section 29 of POCSO Act which provides for presumption as to certain offence.

According to which when a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under section 3, 5, 7, & 9 of the Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed, abetted or attempted to commit the offence as the case may be unless the contrary is proved.
The word employed "contrary to be proved" marks significance, particularly when it pre-supposes in a given case conduction of trial.

Even otherwise the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra and others AIR 2021 SC 1918 had flagged a note of caution wherein certain parameters were enunciated for interference at the stage of Section 482 Cr.P.C./ 528 BNSS.
9.

entities.text: Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra and others AIR 2021 SC 1918
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Cumulatively, analysing the case of four corner of law, this Court does not find the present case to be a fit case for interference in the present proceeding.
Accordingly, no case is made out and the application is hereby rejected.
9. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicants submits that suitable direction be issued to the court below for considering the application of the applicant for enlargement of the bail.
